dialogue.mcacapitals_petition_menu: What do you petition the sovereign for?
dialogue.mcacapitals_petition_noble_menu: What noble dignity do you seek?
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_news_heir_name: There are {royal_child_count} royal children in court now. Figuring out the succession order is its own occupation.
{heir_name} is next in line. {sovereign_name} made it official.
A named heir means less uncertainty. I’m glad of it.
Crown Prince. Crown Princess. The title changes nothing about who they are. But it changes everything about how people see them.
I wonder if {heir_name} wanted it. You never know, with heirs. Sometimes they want it desperately. Sometimes not at all.
Now that we have an heir, I wonder if bethrothal comes next?
The heir looked calm about it. I think that was practiced. Nobody is calm about inheriting a throne.
Now everyone in court is quietly calculating what happens if the heir doesn't make it to the throne.
The heir was called to court earlier. Looked like they knew why.
Someone asked me the succession order. I said to ask someone who enjoys headaches.
They named the heir, then. That explains all the whispering near the hall.
Someone asked me if the line is settled now. I laughed before I meant to.
The heir’s name has been on every tongue today.
People keep saying ‘next in line’ like that makes the rest simple.
The court has been watching {heir_name} differently since morning.
The succession is clear now. So naturally, everyone is still arguing.
{heir_name} was named heir, and now everyone keeps saying ‘the line’ like they understand it.
The heir announcement had the hall quiet for once.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_news_capital_f: They say {capital_name} has a proper sovereign now. Strange to think we were just a village not so long ago.
People keep asking me how I feel about it. Honestly? Safer. A capital needs someone at the top.
{sovereign_name} was chosen from among us. Not some faraway lord. One of our own. That means something.
I never thought I'd live in a capital. And here we are.
The herald's been announcing it all morning. {capital_name} has a sovereign. I imagine the neighbouring villages have heard of it by now.
Some folks weren't sure about the Charter. But what's the alternative? You can't just leave a capital with nobody at the helm.
With {sovereign_name} crowned, things will start to change around here. Whether that's good or not remains to be seen.
A sovereign is one thing. A court is another. Let's see how long before the titles start coming.
I remember when this was just a handful of houses and a well. Look at it now.
Whoever made that decision — to crown someone, to make this official — I hope they knew what they were starting.
I've heard of capitals. Read about them, even. I never thought I'd live in one.
The new sovereign walked through the square this morning as if they'd always been in charge. Maybe they have been, in some ways.
People keep calling it progress. I'm not sure what its progress toward. But I suppose we'll find out.
They’re calling us a capital now. I still saw a pig in the hall this morning.
The sovereign was crowned, and half the village started walking like court mattered yesterday.
The herald was so excited about the announcement, I thought he was going to trip over his own feet.
We needed structure. Whether we needed a throne is a different question. But here we are.
People keep saying {capital_name} feels different now. It does, but the mud is the same.
The Charter has everyone acting busy. Some of them even are.
I heard a villager ask if capitals still need fences. Sensible question.
The first morning as a capital, and the well is still where everyone gets the news.
{capital_name} has been loud all morning. I blame the court until proven otherwise.
The village felt smaller before all these titles arrived.
If you are looking for quiet, you chose the wrong capital.
The square is busy today. Either the court has news, or the market has gossip.
I saw someone sweeping the square before sunrise. That’s new.
A capital, they say. Same mud, better arguments.
Someone asked where the court meets. I said, ‘wherever people are blocking the door.’
The Charter changed the place faster than the builders ever did.
I heard two villagers practicing bows behind the well.
The neighbouring villages will hear about this by supper, if they haven’t already.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_news_royal_mar: A royal marriage is never just a marriage. It's an arrangement. Ask anyone who's been at court long enough.
I saw the consort at the ceremony. A proper royal household now — {sovereign_name} won't be ruling alone.
{capital_name} has been talking since the wedding. I assume it will tire eventually.
Funny how a wedding changes a person's title overnight. One day a subject, the next a consort.
The herald couldn't stop smiling when he made the announcement. You'd think he was the one getting married.
I heard the ceremony was brief. {sovereign_name} doesn't seem the type for ceremony.
A royal spouse means an heir eventually. That's what everyone's really thinking about.
People keep congratulating me as if I had anything to do with it. I just live here.
Word spreads fast in {capital_name}. The gossip had it before the herald did.
The consort stays close to {sovereign_name}. Always. I'm not sure if that's affection or politics.
Someone asked about heirs before the feast was cleared. No shame in this capital.
The wedding announcement gave the herald far too much joy.
The court smiled all through the wedding. I trust that less than arguing.
{capital_name} will be talking about the royal marriage until something louder happens.
The consort has more influence than their title suggests. Anyone who's been paying attention knows that.
Did you hear about the latest Royal Wedding? I sent a gift. Nothing grand, I figured everyone else would send something grand.
They say the couple seems genuinely fond of each other. That's rarer than people admit.
The political implications are what everyone is talking about in private. In public, they're all smiles.
An heir becomes more likely after a royal marriage. Everyone knows it. I’d bet my last emerald that the court is already planning.
The gossip about the wedding has already outlasted the wedding itself.
The wedding’s done, but the market is still talking like it just started.
Someone brought a gift wrapped in wool. I hope that was intentional.
The herald looked far too pleased announcing the marriage.
I heard the vows were short. Good. Some of us had work.
A royal marriage makes everyone suddenly interested in family trees.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_news_sovereign: The court feels hollow right now. That's the only word for it.
I've never seen so many villagers in black at the same time. The whole capital changed overnight.
The sovereign is dead. The hall has not sounded right since.
Black cloth went up before the market even opened.
{capital_name} is {mourning_status}. Even the square knows to keep quiet.
The guards stood closer to the royal rooms after the death.
I saw villagers stop mid-trade when the announcement came.
The court has been moving softly since {sovereign_name} died.
The mourning started before some people had even heard the news.
Someone asked about succession already. I wish I were surprised.
The dowager has my sympathy. I cannot imagine.
If you are going to the hall, speak softly today.
Already, we have a new sovereign. I can’t imagine the pain of all those who were left behind.
The mourning will end in a day or two. The court will carry on. That's what courts do.
The children keep asking when the dark clothes come off.
{capital_name} is {mourning_status}. Whatever comes next, it won't be the same.
They say the succession is already being sorted. Someone had to start planning before the body was even cold.
I kept my original clothes under the mourning cloth. I know that's shameful. But I never really liked black.
I've lived in {capital_name} long enough to see two rulers now. Every time the court shifts, the whole place shifts with it.
The dowager doesn't speak at court much. But when they do, {sovereign_name} listens.
The capital is quieter than I've ever heard it. Even the market sounds muffled somehow.
Nobody is saying much near the royal rooms.
The guards have been standing closer to the doors.
I saw black cloth being carried out before the announcement.
The market went quiet when the herald arrived.
People keep asking who knew first. Strange thing to ask.
The court looks smaller today.
Two days of mourning. That's the rule. It feels both too long and not long enough.
Death in a ruling family doesn't stay private. The whole settlement wears it.
I keep expecting to see the former sovereign wandering around the village, then I remember.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_news_throne_se: Seizing the throne is one thing. Holding it is another. We'll see.
The whole thing was over in moments. But the court is still shaking.
The old royal family is gone from the active line now. Just like that. Years of court life, erased.
I won't say I'm surprised. Anyone paying attention could see how much standing they'd built up.
The commander's support made the difference, they say. Remember that the next time someone tells you the military office is just ceremonial.
I keep wondering what happens to the children. Where do they go when the dynasty falls?
The commander’s name keeps coming up after the coup. I wonder if they knew.
The old royal household passed through the square today. Nobody knew where to look.
After the throne was seized, everyone suddenly found somewhere else to be.
The new sovereign was announced like the whole capital had not already heard.
People are choosing their words carefully since the coup.
The throne changed hands by force, and now every noble looks busy.
Someone asked what side I was on. I was standing near the door.
People keep asking whose side I was on. In truth, I am on the side of whoever wins.
The square emptied faster than I’ve ever seen it.
The herald announced the new sovereign like everyone had not already heard.
People are choosing their words very carefully today.
I saw a noble change direction when they saw the guards.
Every sovereign who has ever lost a throne probably thought it couldn't happen to them.
The herald announced a new ruler this morning. Most people already knew. Word travels fast in {capital_name}.
The new sovereign hasn't spoken publicly yet. The court is very quiet right now.
History remembers coups differently depending on who survives to write them.
Nobody who was there will stop talking about it. Nobody who wasn't there will stop asking.
There are no innocent bystanders in a coup. Everyone was already taking a side; they just didn't know it.
The commander's role in all of this is going to be discussed for years.
History will call it a coup. Whether it calls it a good one or a bad one depends on what comes next, I guess.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_news_disinheri: The decree came down, and that was that. No explanation. No appeal.
One moment, you are a member of the Royal Family. The next, you are simply a name the court no longer dares to say aloud.
People keep asking what happened. Nobody seems to know for certain. Or nobody's willing to say.
It shook the nobles more than anyone expected. Disinheritance reminds everyone that their standing is not guaranteed either.
Did you hear of the disinheritance? People are talking about it, but nobody's talking too loudly. You never know who's listening.
Whatever they did — or whatever the sovereign believed they did — the result is the same.
A disinheritance changes more than one person's future. Everyone in the line moves.
I feel sorry for the family. Whatever the circumstances, this isn't quite grief. It's public.
Someone mentioned the disinheritance by the well and got pulled away by the sleeve.
The disinheritance came down this morning. People stopped using the name very quickly.
The decree removed them from the line, and now the court is pretending not to gossip.
The herald kept the disinheritance announcement short. Wise of them.
The disinheritance has the nobles whispering softer than usual.
People keep saying ‘removed from the line’ like that makes it cleaner.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_news_legitimiz: Did you hear of the recent legitimization? Some of the older courtiers were not pleased. They weren't going to say that out loud, of course.
Legitimization reshapes the succession. Everyone in the line shifts a little.
It's a kind thing, if you think about it. Giving someone a place they didn't have before.
The herald announced it this morning. You could hear the murmuring all the way to the outer buildings.
The court took the announcement of the legitimization more quietly than I expected. Sometimes that's louder than noise.
Did you hear who was just legitimized? Some at court were surprised. Others clearly expected it.
A child recognized by the dynasty is part of the succession now. That changes things for everyone in the line.
The legitimization decree added another royal name today.
Someone asked if the child is royal now. The Maester looked tired already.
The legitimization has the court counting heirs again.
The decree made it official. The gossip was official much earlier.
The royal family tree gained another branch. The Maester will need more ink.
Someone said legitimization is simple. That person has not met this court.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_news_abdicatio: Did you hear about the abdication? I didn't think they would actually do it. But the declaration was signed, and here we are.
Abdication is rare. Most people hold onto power until something takes it from them.
The successor was already named. The transition was almost… smooth. That surprised people.
The court always adjusts eventually. But it takes time after something like this.
A sovereign who steps down is either very wise or very tired. Maybe both.
People keep asking why they abdicated the throne. I'm not sure there's ever one reason for something like that.
Did you hear of the abdication? The herald had a whole speech prepared. Nobody's quite sure what to do with it now.
There's a new ruler in {capital_name}, and the old one is still walking around. That's a strange thing to get used to.
{sovereign_name} doesn't hold court the way the last sovereign did. This one listens more.
I watched the former sovereign walk through the square afterward. They looked lighter, if anything.
Whether the decision was wise or not will depend on what the successor does with the throne.
The abdication has everyone confused about how to address the former sovereign.
The former sovereign crossed the square today. Half the market nearly bowed twice.
After the abdication, the hall filled before breakfast.
People keep saying the abdication was peaceful. They sound surprised.
Does the old Soveregin still get the good chair?
The new reign started before the old one felt finished.
The abdication has the court rearranging itself like furniture.
I saw someone bow to the new sovereign, then turn and bow to the old one too.
Nobody quite knew where to stand during the transition. Court etiquette doesn't cover this often enough.
The court reset faster than I expected. Titles shifted, offices were confirmed, and by evening it was almost normal.
The former sovereign still lives here. I’m not quite sure how to address them. Do I bow? I think I should bow.
A peaceful handover in a capital is extraordinary. I don't think we appreciated it enough in the moment.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_news_new_duke_: Dukedom isn't given lightly. {sovereign_name} must have seen something worth rewarding.
Ducal rank changes how everyone else behaves around a person. Watch — you'll see it within a day.
The herald announced the new dukedom loud enough for the farms.
The court loves a new title. Gives everyone something to misuse.
A new dukedom was bequeathed today. They say the petition was accepted without much debate. {sovereign_name} seemed certain.
Did you hear? Another villager raised to Dukedom. The herald made the announcement. I could hear it from the other end of {capital_name}.
Being a Duke sounds magnificent until you realize how many people are now watching your every move.
I put in a petition once. Long time ago. Never heard back. Some are luckier than others.
I've known them since before they received their title. It's strange to bow to someone you've shared meals with.
Ducal rank is the highest noble title below the royal family. Maybe one day they’ll even be royal themselves.
Did you hear the news? The herald announced it three times. Once would have been enough, but I think they were enjoying it.
Someone became a lord and immediately forgot how doors work.
If a noble asks for directions, give them the long way.
Someone said ‘Your Grace’ to the wrong person. I enjoyed that.
If this is about rank, ask the court. If this is about work, ask anyone else.
The lords have been gathered near the hall. Either news or vanity.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_news_lord_comm: {commander_name} is Lord Commander now. I feel safer already just knowing that.
The military office isn't ceremonial. Not now with {commander_name} in it.
A capital without a commander is nervous. {capital_name} can relax a little now.
Lord Commander. Even the title sounds like armour.
The herald announced {commander_name}, but the barracks seemed to know first.
The guards looked relieved after the Lord Commander was named.
The appointment explains why the road patrols doubled.
A capital with a Lord Commander sleeps a little differently.
The Lord Commander's appointment had every guard standing straighter by noon.
Some of the guards weren't sure how to react at first. Now they seem steadier. A good commander does that.
A court with a Lord Commander is a court that can defend itself. That changes the conversation with everyone outside {capital_name}.
I feel safer knowing the military office is filled. A capital without a commander is vulnerable in ways people don't appreciate until it's too late.
The appointment wasn't surprising. They'd been building toward it for a while.
Lord Commander is a title with real weight. Not just ceremony — genuine battlefield authority.
Did you hear? We have a new Lord Commander. It took a significant petition to earn that office. The standing required isn't easy to build.
The capital feels more organized now. There's a chain of command, and everyone knows their place in it.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_news_hand_of_t: {hand_name} is Hand now. That's real power. More than most titles.
The Hand speaks with {sovereign_name}'s voice when they're not here to address the Capital.
Does that mean that {hand_name} is as powerful as a King, now?
A Hand spends half the day solving problems for {sovereign_name} and the other half preventing new ones.
Being Hand sounds like an honour. I think it's mostly just work.
The court feels more organized with that office of the Hand filled. There's someone to go to now.
I saw {hand_name} speaking with the herald this morning. Something's being prepared. I don't know what.
People said {hand_name} was an odd choice. I think they underestimated them.
The Hand's office being filled is the single best thing that could happen to this court right now.
The new title has everyone practicing how to stand.
I've heard them described as the sovereign's shadow. Personally, I think of them more as the sovereign's spine.
A good Hand prevents more crises than they solve. You never notice the ones they prevent.
The herald went on at some length about the appointment. The new Hand looked mildly embarrassed by the fuss.
Being Hand means being responsible for things that go wrong when no one else claims them. A thankless job done well.
The court has someone proper to blame now that {hand_name} has the office.
The Hand was appointed, and the petitions found them immediately.
The herald announced {hand_name}, and three people left to go bother them.
The Hand’s office is filled. Maybe complaints will stop landing everywhere else.
{hand_name} looked busy before the title. Bad sign for them.
The Hand appointment has the court acting organized. For now.
The appointment required significant trust from the sovereign. You don't give that office to someone you're unsure of.
The court feels different with a Hand in place. Steadier. Like someone finally checked that the foundation was sound.
{hand_name} is Hand now. I saw three people waiting outside their door before breakfast.
The Hand has been walking fast all morning. That usually means the court has made a mess.
Someone brought {hand_name} a petition with soup on it. I wish I were joking.
{hand_title} sounds grand until you see the paperwork.
The Hand’s office is full again. Good. People were starting to bring problems to the rest of us.
The court feels different with a Hand in place. Steadier. Like someone finally checked that the foundation was sound.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_news_grand_mae: They've been a cleric here for years. Now look at them. {grand_maester_name} is the crown’s learned voice.
The appointment was quiet. But the effect on the court wasn't.
{grand_maester_name} doesn't say much in public. The advice goes to {sovereign_name} privately.
Every great court has a scholar at the heart of it. {capital_name} has one now.
We now have a Hand, a Commander, and a Grand Maester. {sovereign_name} is building something serious here.
Whatever wisdom the court needs that isn't military — that's {grand_maester_name}'s domain now.
The cleric has been here longer than most. The title is overdue, if you ask me.
I spoke with the Grand Maester briefly after the ceremony. They seem unchanged by the title, so that's probably a good sign.
Knowledge is the only kind of power that doesn't come with enemies attached. Usually.
{grand_maester_name} is Grand Maester now. The archives finally look supervised.
{sovereign_name} has a Grand Maester. The court may get longer answers.
The appointment was quiet. The Grand Maester probably preferred it that way.
I saw extra paper carried to the archives after the appointment.
The court has a learned voice now. It still has to listen.
The Grand Maester’s first act was correcting a date. Sounds right.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_news_royal_gua: I saw the royal guard follow {sovereign_name} through the Capital earlier today.
I saw two members of the Royal Guard arguing over who gets to stand closest to the sovereign.
I heard the members of the Royal Guard have to follow {sovereign_name} wherever they go. When do they get to sleep?
Royal guards answer only to {sovereign_name}. Nobody else gets to give them orders. Not even the commander, not really.
If {sovereign_name} dies, the guards will be disgraced. How would they survive living here, knowing that?
Three guards for one sovereign seems like a lot. I hope it’s not our taxes paying for that.
Did you hear? Three guards were named to the Royal Guard. The herald announced the appointment this morning.
There's a reason the guard position requires real standing to appoint. You don't put just anyone that close to a sovereign.
Someone tried to call over the royal guard. That went nowhere.
I heard there can only be three royal guards.
The appointment was short, but the guards looked like they had stopped breathing.
The old guards watched the new royal guard very closely.
The royal guard has a different walk already.
{sovereign_name} has another guard close now. The square noticed.
The royal guard appointment made the ordinary guards very quiet.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_news_peaceful_: The petition route is harder than it looks. You don't build that kind of standing in a week.
The old sovereign stepped back graciously. I wasn't sure they would. I was wrong about them.
No blades, no blood, just a great many careful faces.
The old sovereign stepped aside, and every courtier tried to look like they expected it.
The throne changed hands without anyone drawing steel. I did not know we did that here.
The petition for the throne worked. That will make half the capital ambitious by morning.
The former sovereign stood there while the new one was named. Hard room to breathe in.
People looked relieved after the peaceful transfer, then immediately confused.
{capital_name} has a new ruler, and nobody had to draw anything to make it happen.
The former sovereign's title is gone now. Their household, too. The court moves on quickly.
People said you couldn't take a throne without a fight. {sovereign_name} proved them wrong.
The herald had to announce a new ruler with the old ruler still in the room. I don't imagine that was comfortable for anyone.
Building that kind of favour takes patience. {sovereign_name} was patient.
I never thought I'd see a throne change hands without something being broken.
It takes an unusual kind of character to give up a throne willingly. The former sovereign has my respect.
Building that kind of standing takes years. Most people give up before they get close.
I think the former sovereign was relieved. There's a kind of weight that comes off a person when the burden passes to someone else.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_news_royal_bir: Everyone’s asking if it’s a prince or princess. I’m asking if the mother’s alright.
The herald said the name twice. Still didn’t catch it.
Another royal child. The court will be counting again.
I heard the baby cried through the whole announcement.
The royal rooms have been busy all morning.
A new royal child, and already people are counting who stands where.
I heard the baby cried louder than the announcement.
Someone already started talking succession. The child’s barely here.
The royal household needed more noise, apparently.
{capital_name} has been talking about the baby all morning.
That makes {royal_child_count} royal children now, if I’ve counted right.
That baby has more titles near it than I have boots.
{capital_name} does love a royal birth.
{herald_name} announced it loud enough for the cows.
{sovereign_name} has a new child. The whole capital’s been counting fingers and titles.
{consort_name} looked exhausted after the birth. Anyone with sense kept their congratulations brief.
{heir_name} has a new little shadow in the line. That should keep the court busy.
{consort_name} looked exhausted. Anyone who gave a long speech deserves a glare.
{sovereign_name} has a new child. Everyone has already decided who the baby looks like.
The new royal child is in the chronicle before most of us learned the name.
That makes {royal_child_count} royal children now. Someone check my count.
The market has been talking about the baby all morning. Nobody agrees on who it looks like.
The royal household has {royal_household_count} people in it now. No wonder the hall is always noisy.
I saw a guard carrying blankets to the royal rooms. Looked more nervous than during a raid.
Someone asked about succession before the child was even named. Some people have no shame.
The baby cried through the royal birth announcement. Good start, honestly.
The royal household has {royal_household_count} people now. The hall will not be quiet again.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_news_court_her: The new herald’s got lungs, I’ll give them that.
The new herald’s got a voice on them. I heard the appointment from inside my house.
They picked {herald_name} for Court Herald. Good lungs, that one.
{herald_name} announced their own appointment. Strange way to start a job, but they managed.
The court has a herald again. Maybe now the gossip will at least have competition.
I heard {herald_name} practicing by the well. Half the village heard it too.
The herald’s office is filled now. That should keep {latest_event} from being told five different ways.
{herald_name} was named Court Herald. The square will never know peace again.
The herald appointment explains all the shouting by the well this morning.
{herald_name} has the office now. Good voice, dangerous confidence.
The well-gossipers looked offended when the new herald started.
The Court Herald is named. Now the news can arrive loudly instead of merely wrong.
{herald_name} has been named Court Herald. I hope they know how to pronounce all those titles.
{herald_name} is Court Herald now. Good voice. Hard to escape.
The new herald practiced by the well this morning. Half of {capital_name} heard the warmup.
The herald’s office is filled again. Good. People were starting to invent their own announcements.
The new herald started before everyone had turned around.
{herald_name} has been given a title and has decided to use the whole voice.
The court has a herald again. The well-gossipers looked offended.
I hope the new herald likes repeating things. People never listen the first time.
The appointment was announced loudly enough to scare the chickens.
{herald_name} knows how to make people stop walking. I’ll give them that.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_news_mourning_: {capital_name} is out of mourning now. The streets look less heavy.
The herald announced the end of mourning at first light. Kept it short, for once.
Two days in black felt longer than two days. I’m glad to see colour again.
The market sounded more like itself this morning. Not all the way, but closer.
Someone laughed in the square, then looked around like they’d broken a law.
{herald_name} announced the end of mourning at first light. No grand speech, thankfully.
People are speaking normally again. Mostly.
I saw someone put their mourning clothes away and stand there a while.
The square has colour in it again.
It feels strange seeing the guards in regular dress again.
The market got louder today, but not by much.
The herald announced the end of mourning without making a meal of it.
The mourning cloth is folded away now. The guards still look like it isn’t.
The tailor has had a strange week, with all that mourning cloth.
The mourning period is done. The hall is still learning how to sound normal.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_capital_topic_: People are still talking about {latest_event}. I imagine they will be for a while yet.
A capital this size generates politics whether you want it to or not.
{capital_population} people in {capital_name} now. Every day there's someone new I don't recognize.
The chronicle records more than most people realize. It's worth reading, if you get the chance.
Someone bowed to the wrong person today. I am trying not to enjoy it.
Half the capital has news. The other half has better news.
The well knows more secrets than the council.
People are walking too quickly today. That usually means an announcement is coming.
Someone should tell the nobles that doors are for entering, not whispering beside.
If you hear shouting, wait. If you hear silence, leave.
I miss when gossip only needed two names.
Court gossip moves faster than the herald's announcements. Always has.
The herald's name is {herald_name}. And yes, they are exactly as loud as you'd expect from someone in that role.
Some folks resent the titles. Others want one desperately. I recommend keeping your head down.
With {royal_household_count} people in the royal household, the palace is never empty.
Every time something changes in the court, I hear about it before the morning is out. This place cannot keep a secret.
{heir_name} carries that title like a weight. You can see it.
People are always watching the royal children. Waiting to see who becomes what.
I heard {heir_name} arguing with one of the guards. Not about anything serious. But it was strange to see the heir looking so ordinary.
The royal household has {royal_household_count} people in it now. It runs like a small village on its own.
The court keeps inventing ways to make standing in a room complicated.
Someone asked if a knight outranks a lord. I suddenly had somewhere to be.
A new title always makes the square louder.
If {latest_event} involves a title, give the gossip until supper.
Someone became a lord and immediately forgot how doors work.
If a noble asks for directions, give them the long way.
Someone said ‘Your Grace’ to the wrong person. I enjoyed that.
If this is about rank, ask the court. If this is about work, ask anyone else.
The lords have been gathered near the hall. Either news or vanity.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_commoner_: People used to gossip about trades. Now it’s titles.
Every villager in {capital_name} has an opinion now.
The herald’s been busy since {latest_event}.
I don’t know who outranks whom. I just know who gets bowed to.
Someone asked if I’d petition for a title. I said I like sleeping.
I know enough court business to avoid court business.
If the sovereign wants my opinion, I’ll be in the field.
A royal family is still a family. They argue. They disagree. They just do it in nicer rooms.
The children of {sovereign_name} will inherit a different {capital_name} than the one that was chartered. Whether that's better or worse is yet to be seen.
I think {heir_name} will be a good ruler someday. They ask more questions than most people expect an heir to ask.
I'm not nobility. I'm not a guard. I live here, I work here, and I watch what happens.
{sovereign_name} seems like a fair ruler so far, but we’ll see how that holds.
I couldn't tell you the full succession order, but I know {heir_name} is next in line. Everyone knows that much.
I used to know everyone here. Now I know everyone’s title instead.
Someone asked me who I support. I said the person paying fair for wheat.
I do not mind the court, so long as it stays mostly over there.
A guard told me to clear the road. I was already clearing it.
The nobles talk like the rest of us do not have ears.
I know enough about succession to know I want no part of it.
The capital got bigger. My house did not.
If the herald wants me, they can shout. They usually do.
I liked it when the biggest argument was over trade prices.
People ask me if I'd ever petition for a title. I don't have the standing. Or the patience.
{capital_name} is bigger than it was. Some days that feels like progress, most of the time it just feels crowded.
The latest news — {latest_event} — hasn't changed my daily life much. But the court seems to think it matters enormously.
I don't follow politics. Politics follows me. That's what living in a capital teaches you.
I couldn't tell you the full title hierarchy if you paid me. I know who matters, though.
I saw the royal guard pass through the market today. Impressive. Also a little unsettling.
A capital is a village that got ambitious. I say that with affection.
People keep asking if I want to petition for something. I want to live quietly and not be noticed. That's my petition.
Whatever happened in the court this week, I heard about it before the announcement. Gossip is faster than heralds.
I think the sovereign is doing well. I base that on almost no information and a general feeling. I think that's how most people do it.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_knight_01: Sir is a title. The sword work behind it is what actually matters.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_knight_02: I earned this rank through the guard path. I am proud of it.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_knight_03: A knight without discipline is just a soldier with a fancier name.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_knight_04: My position allows me to visit every building in the Capital. I know every road in and out of {capital_name}, and everyone in it.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_knight_05: I was knighted in {capital_name}. This is my home. I will defend it as such.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_knight_06: People think the knightly rank is ceremonial. Come stand watch on a raid night and tell me that.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_knight_07: Sir. Dame. The title marks what we do and who we serve. I think that is as it should be.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_knight_08: The regular knights respect the guard. Most of them, anyway. The ones who don't learn quickly.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_knight_09: I have stood through mourning, through celebration, through raids. The guard does not stop for any of it.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_knight_10: This is the most important role I will ever hold in {capital_name}. I intend to hold it without fault.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_knight_11: The knightly rank means I am part of this court's defence in a way that goes beyond standing watch.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_knight_12: I serve the court, the capital, and the sovereign. In all three directions at once, most days.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_knight_13: The Commander wants the west path watched. So I am watching it.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_knight_14: I checked the gate twice already. I will check it again.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_knight_15: If someone says they are allowed through, send them to me first.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_knight_16: A quiet road is still a road worth guarding.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_knight_17: I do not mind rain on watch. I mind people complaining at me in it.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_knight_18: If the royal guard passes, give them room.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_knight_19: The bowstring was fine this morning. I checked.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_knight_20: Stay behind the line if there is trouble. No, the line is not a suggestion.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_knight_21: A knight without discipline isn't a knight. That's the first thing you learn when you earn the title.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_knight_22: People who have never stood a night watch don't quite understand what the knightly order does. I don't resent that. Much.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_knight_23: I would rather earn respect than be given it. The title is given. The respect I work for daily.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_lord_comm: The royal household has {royal_household_count} members now. I try to know all of them by name.
I have seen {capital_name} change more than once. I will see it change again.
The military of {capital_name} is my responsibility. I take that personally.
A commander who is not feared a little is not doing the job correctly.
Every guard in this capital is an extension of my word. I choose those words carefully.
{capital_name} has had commanders before me. I intend to be the one they compare future commanders to.
My role in a coup attempt is not something I take lightly. The sovereign's safety is the priority. Always.
When the capital is {mourning_status}, the guard does not stand down. Mourning is when you are most vulnerable.
People who have never stood a night watch don't quite understand what the knightly order does. I don't resent that. Much.
I would rather earn respect than be given it. The title is given. The respect I work for daily.
Command is not given. It is maintained every single day.
A capital without military leadership is a capital that doesn't know how fragile it is.
I have held this position through quiet periods and through raids. Neither is as simple as it looks from the outside.
My standard for the guard is high. I know it. They know it. We've found an understanding.
Lord Commander is a title that carries history with it. I looked into that history before I accepted the office.
A good commander is not always a visible one. Prevention is the measure, not response.
When the capital is at risk, the sovereign looks to me. I have no interest in disappointing them.
Tell the east guard I want the post changed before dusk.
The royal guard reports first. Everyone else waits.
If the sovereign leaves the hall, I want to know which road.
Do not crowd the gate. It makes everyone slower.
I want the archers where they can see, not where they look impressive.
If someone says it is nothing, send them to me.
No one stands alone on raid night. Make sure they know that.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_lord_or_l: The master professionals of {capital_name} are the foundation of this court. I came from among them.
People bring me concerns that they won't bring to the higher nobility. I consider that a privilege.
{capital_name} is my home before it is my domain. I try to remember the difference.
There are titles higher than mine. There are responsibilities greater than mine. I do not envy them.
{sovereign_name} can rely on the lords and ladies of this court. I intend to make sure that is true.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_lord_or_L: A lordship is an entry into the politics of this court. I went in with eyes open.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_lord_or_l: People I've known for years now address me differently. It is strange to get used to.
There is real work in this role. More than people outside the court realize.
I remember what this capital was before it had titles. Some days that perspective is more useful than any rank.
If this is a complaint, speak plainly. I hear enough polished nonsense.
I was easier to find before I had a title.
Bring the matter to me before bringing it to the Hand.
Half of being noble is knowing when to stop talking.
The court has been busy today. I have avoided most of it with skill.
If you need a witness, ask before the argument starts.
A title gets you into the room. It does not make the room pleasant.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_duke_or_d: {sovereign_name} bestowed this rank. I serve it by making their court stronger.
Ducal rank comes with expectation. The petition I filed was only the beginning.
I advise where I can. I defer where I should. That balance is the whole job.
The latest development in {capital_name} — {latest_event} — has implications for the nobility that most haven't thought through yet.
I have held this title long enough to know it means nothing without the work behind it.
Lords and knights look to the dukes for signals. I try to make sure the signals I send are worth following.
My responsibility is to {capital_name}. The title is just the shape that responsibility takes.
Some who hold this rank rest on it. I have never understood that. {sovereign_name} elevated me for a reason.
Being elevated changes how people see you. It does not change who you are. That part is still your choice.
I have more standing in this court than I ever expected to reach. It comes with more to answer for.
I advise. I support. I serve. The title makes that sound grander than it sometimes feels.
If the lords are gathering, someone should ask why before they decide.
No, I am not bringing that to the sovereign yet.
I heard the petition. I did not hear a plan.
Tell the new lord to stop bowing at me in doorways.
If the court wants my answer today, it should have asked yesterday.
I will attend the hall when the hall stops attracting fools.
A duchy comes with many visitors. Few are welcome.
If it concerns my standing, say so. We can both save time.
A Duke who forgets that they serve the capital and not the other way around is a problem waiting to happen.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_heir_01: {sovereign_name} carries more than people realize. I try to make sure some of that weight is shared.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_heir_02: The court sees me as an extension of {sovereign_name}. I try to be worthy of that association.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_heir_03: I have no sceptre, no petition rights, no formal power of decree. And yet {capital_name} is different because I am here.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_heir_04: Everything I do in {capital_name} is watched. I stopped pretending otherwise a long time ago.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_heir_05: {sovereign_name} chose me. I try every day to deserve that.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_heir_06: Being heir is not the same as being sovereign. But it is preparation for it. I try to treat it that way.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_heir_07: The succession is clear. I am {heir_title}, heir to the Throne of {capital_name}. What comes after that is not up to me to decide alone.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_heir_08: If this is about succession, I would rather talk about literally anything else.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_heir_09: If they are looking for me, tell them I am not hiding. Not well, anyway.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_heir_10: Someone asked what I would do as ruler. I asked what they wanted.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_heir_11: I know where I stand in the line. Everyone keeps reminding me.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_heir_12: The Maester gave me reading. The Commander gave me warnings. Balanced day.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_heir_13: If the sovereign asks, I was listening.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_heir_14: I do not need another lesson on posture today.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_heir_15: There are {royal_child_count} of us in the royal line. I am simply the one who is next.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_heir_16: People ask me what kind of ruler I will be. I think the honest answer is: I do not know yet. I hope a good one.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_heir_17: The chronicle will have my name in it for a long time. I think about that more than I probably should.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_heir_18: {capital_name} will change between now and when I rule. I try to prepare for a future I cannot fully see.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_heir_19: I try not to think too much about what inheriting the throne actually means. Then I think about it anyway.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_heir_20: An heir is a promise the dynasty makes to the future. I try to be a promise worth keeping.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_heir_21: I asked an old advisor once what the hardest part of ruling was. She said: making decisions when you're not sure. I think about that often.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_heir_22: Some heirs spend their whole life waiting. I would rather spend mine learning.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_heir_23: The court sees the title. I hope, eventually, they also see the person.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_heir_24: Succession is a line drawn in ink. It feels much more fragile than that.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_heir_25: If I inherit this capital, I want to have earned it before I ever sit in the seat.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_royal_chi: People sometimes forget the consort has ears. That is their mistake.
I am a child of {sovereign_name}. That is a fact that shapes every room I walk into.
The heir is {heir_name}. I have made peace with that. Mostly.
Growing up in a royal household means learning that politics is just family with higher stakes.
{capital_name} is my home. Not just my birthplace — my home. I intend to serve it.
If the tutor asks, you have not seen me.
The guards never answer the interesting questions.
I know where the old stairs go. I am not telling.
The herald says my name too loudly.
If I am late, blame the Maester. The book was heavy.
I asked why people bow. Everyone gave a different answer.
The throne room is colder than it looks.
The dynasty is only as strong as the people in it.
I know the succession order. I know where I stand in it. I choose not to think about it too often.
If I inherit this capital, I want to have earned it before I ever sit in the seat.
There are more of us than people sometimes remember. The court has a lot of names to keep straight.
I was born into a title. I'd like to think I'm building something beyond it.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_sovereign: Every decision I make in {capital_name} will be written into the chronicle eventually.
{heir_name} is my named heir. Spread the word, I want no confusion when the time comes.
{commander_name} keeps the court safe. I trust that completely, and I say it publicly because trust should not be assumed.
The court reflects the sovereign. If {capital_name} is uneasy, I am asking myself why.
I have {royal_child_count} children. Each of them will be prepared for whatever role the dynasty asks of them.
{capital_name} did not always have a sovereign. The people who built it without one deserve to be remembered.
People are not sure how to speak to me now. I understand. I am not sure either, sometimes.
A crown is not something you put on. It is something you grow into. I am still growing.
The court reflects the sovereign. When I am uncertain, I can feel it spread outward.
Every decision I make here will outlast the moment I make it. I try to remember that.
My heir knows the weight they will carry. I have been honest with them about it.
I did not expect the loneliness of it. That is the part nobody tells you.
I hold this throne by choice. That means I hold it by responsibility too.
If this is urgent, start with the part where it became urgent.
Tell the Hand I have seen the petition. No, not that one. The other one.
The Commander wants more guards at the gate. I am inclined to agree.
If the herald is looking for me, ask whether they need me or only my title.
If the heir is missing, check the Maester first. Then the stables.
The chronicle can wait until after the decision is made.
I will hear the matter in the hall. Not in the doorway.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_hand_01: If it begins with ‘small matter,’ it is never a small matter.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_hand_02: Someone brought me a petition with soup on it. I am choosing patience.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_hand_03: {sovereign_name} wants this settled before nightfall. Naturally, everyone waited until the afternoon to inform me.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_hand_04: My title is {hand_title}. Most days that means being interrupted by people who say they are sorry.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_hand_05: No, that does not need to reach {sovereign_name}. Not yet.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_hand_06: If the sovereign has already answered, why is this on my desk?
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_hand_07: I need three names, one witness, and fewer opinions.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_hand_08: Tell the herald I approved the short version.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_hand_09: If this matter can wait, prove it by leaving.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_hand_10: No, I am not taking that to the sovereign during supper.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_hand_11: The court is not confused. The court is avoiding being clear.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_hand_12: Walk with me. I can listen or stand still, not both.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_hand_13: I need {commander_name}, two witnesses, and a room with fewer people in it.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_hand_15: If the sovereign asks, I handled it. If anyone else asks, I am handling it.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_hand_16: You need the sovereign? Try the hall first. If they are not there, try wherever the trouble is.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_hand_17: I can speak with you, but not for long. People start lining up if I stand still.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_hand_18: If this is about a petition, leave it on the desk. If it is urgent, tell me why before I decide it is not.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_hand_19: The title sounds grand, yes. Mostly, it means people find me when they do not know who else to bother.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_hand_20: No, the sovereign has not ignored your request. I am the delay, apparently.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_hand_21: If you see the herald, tell them I have not forgotten. I am avoiding them with purpose.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_hand_22: I liked this job better before I understood it.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_hand_23: Walk with me if you need something. I am late to three places already.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_hand_24: {capital_name} has {capital_population} people now, and somehow every complaint still fits on my desk.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_hand_25: The royal household has {royal_household_count} people in it. That is not a household; that is a second court.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_grand_mae: The chronicle is not a coaster. I have said this more than once.
I asked for quiet, not a procession.
That book is older than your title. Hold it properly.
I can advise {sovereign_name}. I cannot make them listen.
The royal household has {royal_household_count} people. That is a great many headaches.
If you are here about a cough, sit down. If you are here about court business, sit down farther away.
People ask for my advice and then look offended when it is advice.
No, I do not know whether the dream meant anything. Eat something and sleep properly.
If you are bleeding, sit. If you are complaining, stand over there.
I need ink, quiet, and someone to stop opening that door.
The record says what happened. Not what people wish happened.
The chronicle is not missing. It is exactly where careless people do not look.
If the child swallowed something, start with what.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_royal_con: I married {sovereign_name}. I did not marry every argument in {capital_name}, though some days it feels close.
When {sovereign_name} says they are fine, I usually start asking better questions.
Some days I miss being addressed by my name before my title.
The royal children are easier to manage than the courtiers. At least children admit when they want something.
If you need a favour, start honestly. I get enough polished nonsense in the hall.
The guard at the door has been standing there all morning. I hope someone remembered to feed them.
The nursery is louder than the council chamber today. Better arguments, too.
If this is about the sovereign, ask clearly. I have had enough careful questions for one morning.
{sovereign_name} missed breakfast again. If {hand_name} asks, I tried.
The royal children have been running through {capital_name} like the guards are obstacles.
{sovereign_name} has been in the hall all morning. Send food before sending more questions.
If this is about {latest_event}, ask plainly. Everyone keeps circling it like a nervous chicken.
Have you seen the sovereign? They were supposed to be in the hall.
If you see the Hand, tell them I am not ignoring them. Not on purpose.
Have you seen {sovereign_name}? They were meant to be in the hall.
If the herald asks, I am not giving another statement today.
No, I do not know where the sovereign put the scepter.
If the royal children are in the square, send them back before the Commander notices.
The hall has been noisy all day. That usually means nobody wants to decide first.
Tell {sovereign_name} I am waiting by the royal rooms. Not patiently, but waiting.
{sovereign_name} said this would be a quiet morning. I believed them for some reason.
If this is for {sovereign_name}, give it to {hand_name}. They know where everything ends up.
If {hand_name} asks, I did tell {sovereign_name} about it.
{capital_name} heard about the wedding faster than some of my friends did.
The guards keep asking where the sovereign went. I was hoping they knew.
Someone asked if the sovereign was in a good mood. That is not a question I answer in public.
The royal rooms have been busy since dawn.
If you need {sovereign_name}, try the hall first. Then try wherever the noise is.
{hand_name} has been looking for the sovereign. That usually means I should be looking too.
If this is about {latest_event}, start with the part that affects the household.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_royal_dow: Have you seen the children? They were meant to stay near the hall.
If this is about the old sovereign, ask plainly.
The herald nearly used my old title today. Nearly.
The hall still feels wrong after mourning. Too much space in the wrong places.
{heir_name} was meant to visit after court. Send them to me if you see them.
The royal children know where I sit. Everyone else makes a ceremony of finding me.
If {hand_name} needs old records, tell them to ask before moving everything.
Someone asked if I still attend court. I said I had not left.
There are {royal_child_count} royal children now. Someone should make sure they are all accounted for.
The young nobles whisper too close to open doors.
After {latest_event}, everyone kept looking toward the royal rooms.
The court has changed since {sovereign_name}. Of course it has. That is what courts do.
If the herald asks, I heard the announcement. Everyone heard the announcement.
Tell the heir I kept the book they asked for.
The guards still nod at the old door. I appreciate that.
If they are moving records again, tell them not to stack them by year. It never works.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_general_player: Your Majesty. I didn't hear you coming.
I heard what you did during the last raid. The guard, the commander, the whole court held. That's your doing.
You built this. Not just the title — the court. The household. The whole thing.
Ruling a capital is different from running a village, or so I'm told. I imagine you're finding that out.
Other settlements have heard about what you've built here. Word travels.
I don't say this to every sovereign. But I think you're a good one. For what that's worth.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_general_succes: You know, I wasn't sure about you when you first arrived. I'm coming around.
That's actually a fair point. I hadn't thought of it that way.
If you are heading to the square, the market already knows.
Someone asked if you would hear petitions today. I told them I value my life too much to guess.
The court has been waiting on you. It is trying to look patient.
Your Majesty, if this is a quiet visit, you chose a loud capital.
The Commander was looking for you earlier. Calmly, which made it worse.
The people noticed what you did during the raid. They are still talking about it.
I appreciate someone who listens as well as they speak. You'd be surprised how rare that is.
You've a good head on your shoulders. I'll give you that.
Come back and talk to me again sometime. I mean that.
Most people walk past without a word. I'm glad you didn't.
Honestly, that's exactly what I needed to hear today.
I trust you a little more than I did this morning. You should know that.
You're observant. I respect observant people.
I've been in this capital a long time. Good conversation is not as common as it should be.
That was well said. Well said indeed.
You've got more sense than most who wander in here and start talking.
The sovereign passed through the square earlier. Everyone suddenly remembered their manners.
If the herald is in the square, someone has either died, married, or been promoted.
The sovereign was speaking with the Commander earlier. The guards looked busy after.
The herald has been warming up their voice again. We are all doomed.
Someone brought the sovereign three petitions before noon. Greedy.
I saw {sovereign_name} near the market. The market behaved itself for once.
If the sovereign is asking for the chronicle, something is being remembered.
I'll speak well of you. To whoever asks.
You understand this capital better than most who've lived here longer.
I like you. It took a moment, but I like you.
Say what you will about newcomers — you've got better manners than half the court.
If {herald_name} says ‘by order’ one more time, the chickens may learn court law.
The square is busy today. Either the court has news, or the market has gossip.
Someone should tell the nobles that whispering beside a well does not make them private.
If you hear shouting from the court, give it a moment. Sometimes that is just how they agree.
The market has been strange today. Too many people pretending not to listen.
{capital_name} has been loud all morning. I blame the court until proven otherwise.
Someone asked if I understood the court hierarchy. I said I understood enough to step aside.
The royal guard passed through the market. Even the animals got out of the way.
The guards are moving differently today. I would stay near the square.
If {commander_name} is counting arrows, do not interrupt.
If a guard tells you to move, move first and ask after.
If there is a raid, find the Commander. Or find someone who already found the Commander.
The royal guard followed {sovereign_name} through the square. Tight formation today.
The heir was called to court earlier. Looked like they knew why.
If the children are near the square, send them back before the guards start counting.
There are {royal_child_count} royal children now. The tutors deserve better pay.
If you see a wooden sword near the hall, do not step on it. Royal trouble.
The children were meant to stay near the royal rooms. They rarely agree with ‘meant to.’
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_capital_fail_0: I'm going to pretend that didn't happen for both our sakes.
Was that meant to be charming? I'm asking seriously.
If you touch the chronicle with muddy hands, the Maester will find you.
If this is about court business, ask someone wearing cleaner boots.
I've had more stimulating conversations with the livestock.
I don't know what you were trying to say, but you didn't say it.
Please don't take this personally, but I'd rather be elsewhere right now.
I'll remember this conversation. As a warning.
You've managed to make me feel worse about my day. Impressive, in a bleak sort of way.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_capital_fail_1: If you are looking for quiet, you chose the wrong capital.
Next time, perhaps say nothing. Nothing tends to go over well.
I'm going to need a moment before I can look at you without irritation.
I gave you my time, and that's what I got in return. Noted.
Some people just shouldn't start conversations. You may be one of them.
I've met people from every corner of this region. You are uniquely unpleasant.
I don't know what you thought that would accomplish.
I'm going to walk away now, and we're both going to be better for it.
You should know that word travels quickly in a capital. Just something to think about.
You've a talent for saying the wrong thing at the wrong moment.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_capital_fail_2: I was willing to like you. You made that very difficult.
Whoever raised you forgot a few things about courtesy.
I don't wish you ill. I simply wish you were elsewhere.
That's going to cost you in this capital. People talk.
Good day. And I mean that as a dismissal, not a farewell.
If this is about court business, ask someone wearing cleaner boots.
